cards.text: This is a psalm of David, Israel's king, and wicked and deceitful mouths are speaking lies against him. It's like finding a group chat that's ALL about you, and every single message is a lie. So David prays, “O God of my praise, be not silent.”

cards.question: These lying mouths surround David with hateful words and attack him. What reason does David say they have?

cards.text: Then David says it plainly: “In return for my love they accuse me…”

cards.question: David is being accused in return for his love. How does David describe himself in the middle of it?

cards.text: They repay him evil for good, and hatred for his love. That's like baking somebody a WHOLE batch and getting the empty box thrown back at your head.
Then the psalm suddenly turns. It stops talking about “they” and starts praying about one man, “him,” and friend, buckle up.

cards.question: The prayer asks for a wicked man to be set over this man. Who should stand at this man's right hand?
When this man is tried, the prayer asks that he be found ___, and that even his prayer count as sin.

cards.text: Friend, this prayer does NOT hold back. It asks that his days be few and another take his position, then it reaches his family: his wife a widow, his children fatherless beggars wandering far from their ruined homes.

cards.question: The prayer comes for this man's belongings next. It asks that a creditor seize all he owns.
The prayer asks that someone show favor to this man's fatherless children.

cards.text: It reaches down the generations: may his descendants be cut off and their name blotted out. May his fathers' iniquity and his mother's sin stay before the LORD.

cards.question: Then the prayer gives a reason. This man never thought to ___ kindness.

cards.text: And it gets worse. He pursued the poor and needy and brokenhearted, even to their death.

cards.question: This man loved cursing and refused to delight in blessing. What does the prayer ask?

answers.text: That cursing fall on him and blessing stay far away
That he finally learn to delight in blessing
That all his cursing be forgiven and forgotten

cards.text: Then comes a picture: he wore cursing like a coat, and the prayer asks it to soak into his body like water and into his bones like oil. Friend, I've worn this apron so long I don't know where it ends and I begin.

cards.question: The prayer pictures this man's cursing like a belt tied around him forever.

cards.text: Then David ties the whole thing together. He asks that all of this be the LORD's reward to certain people.

cards.question: Who does David ask the LORD to repay this way?

answers.text: His accusers who speak evil against him
Everyone in Israel who breaks the law
The nations that march against Israel

cards.text: Then David turns back to God, and the whole tone changes: “But You, O GOD, the Lord, deal kindly with me for the sake of Your name; deliver me by the goodness of Your loving devotion.”

cards.question: David asks God to deliver him. What reason does David give about himself?

cards.text: David says he's fading away like a lengthening shadow, his knees weak from fasting, his body lean and gaunt. Friend, I know fading: after years in that junk drawer, I was basically dust with a mustache.

cards.question: David is weak and fading. When his accusers see him, they scorn him and shake their heads at him.

cards.text: So David cries out again: “Help me, O LORD my God; save me according to Your loving devotion.”

cards.question: David asks the LORD to save him. What does David want his accusers to know?

answers.text: That the LORD has done it
That David is stronger than them

cards.question: David tells God that even though his accusers curse, “You will ___.”

cards.text: David says when his accusers rise up, they'll be put to shame, but the LORD's servant will rejoice. The man they've been shaking their heads at will be the one REJOICING.

cards.question: Earlier, the man being prayed against wore cursing like a coat. Now David prays that his accusers will be clothed with disgrace and wear their shame like a ___.

cards.text: Remember how David opened, asking God not to be silent? Now David makes a promise about his own mouth.

cards.question: David promises to praise the LORD quietly where no one else can hear.

cards.text: Then David gives the reason he'll praise the LORD. And it's a good one.

cards.question: Earlier, the prayer asked for an accuser to stand at the right hand of the man being prayed against. Who does David say stands at the right hand of the needy one?

cards.text: The LORD is there to save him from the condemners of his soul. The psalm starts with David surrounded by hateful words and ends with the LORD standing at the right hand of the needy, and friend, I'd take that trade EVERY single time.
